params.content:
# Local Language Models on Android — Current State Research

## 1. llama.cpp on Android
- Runs GGUF quantized models (Q4_K_M, Q8_0, etc.) via NDK build; popular frontends: llama.cpp terminal build, Termux, and apps like LocalAI, ChatterUI, PalM.
- Memory: roughly (parameter count × bytes per weight after quantization) + ~0.5–1.5 GB runtime overhead. Typical examples reported by users:
  - 1–3B models at Q4 (~0.6–2 GB RAM) run comfortably on 6–8 GB phones.
  - 7–8B at Q4 (~4.5 GB) needs an 8–12 GB device, often with heavy RAM pressure/background app kills.
  - 13B+ generally impractical on phones.
- Speed (community reports, Snapdragon 8 Gen 2/3, CPU-only): ~8–15 tok/s for 7–8B Q4; 20–40+ tok/s for 1–3B models. Vulkan backend gives a notable uplift.

## 2. MediaPipe LLM Inference API
- Google's bundled runtime (GPU/NNAPI delegate), ships Gemma-2B (1B/2B-it), Falcon, and converts to MediaPipe .task / LLM bundle format.
- Memory: Gemma-2B (~2.6 GB with int8 / ~1.7 GB int4) reported on Pixel 8; total app footprint commonly 2–4 GB for 2B-class models.
- Speed: Google reports roughly 20–40 tok/s on flagship Tensor/Snapdragon GPUs for 2B-class models, faster prefill on GPU delegate; slower than llama.cpp on some mid-range CPUs but smoother on flagship GPUs.

## 3. Real-world numbers people report
- Small models (0.5–1B, e.g. SmolLM2, Qwen2.5-0.5B): 40–100+ tok/s, ~0.5–1 GB RAM — very usable.
- 3B class (Llama 3.2 3B, Qwen2.5-3B): 15–30 tok/s, 2–3.5 GB RAM.
- 7–8B Q4 (Llama 3.1 8B, Gemma 7/9B): 6–15 tok/s, 4.5–6 GB RAM — usable but tight on 8 GB phones.
- Larger than 8B: generally not viable; users resort to cloud offload.

## 4. Framework comparison
- llama.cpp: widest model choice, best CPU performance, Vulkan GPU support; setup more technical.
- MediaPipe LLM: easiest Android integration, good GPU delegate, limited model selection (mainly Gemma/Falcon).
- MLC LLM / WebLLM: Vulkan/OpenCL GPU execution, good speed on Adreno/Mali, model zoo limited.
- Key bottleneck: memory bandwidth (LPDDR5X ~50–70 GB/s) rather than compute; quantization to 4-bit is standard practice.

## 5. Practical guidance
- 8 GB RAM phone → comfortably run up to 3B Q4; 7–8B only with aggressive quantization and no background apps.
- 12–16 GB RAM phones → 8B Q4 is realistic at ~8–15 tok/s.
- Best tok/s per GB RAM: 0.5–3B quantized models; these are the sweet spot for on-device chat in 2025–2026.

_Note: figures are aggregated from community benchmarks and docs (llama.cpp GitHub, MediaPipe docs, XDA/reddit reports) and vary by device, backend, and quantization._

Running: search why android 14 background services get killed aggressively even with battery optimization turned off and what workaround developers recommend (1 steps)
• Execute CHAT

**Why Android 14 kills background services aggressively — even with battery optimization off — and what developers recommend** **Root causes** 1. **Cached app (OOM) adj limits.** Battery optimization ("Unrestricted" in the settings) only exempts an app from *Doze/App Standby* — it does **not** change the process lifecycle. Android still limits total cached processes and kills background processes first to keep foreground RAM available. On 8 GB-and-under devices Android 14 tightened the LMKD (low memory killer) thresholds and the `cached apps` quota, so a background service hosted by a killed *process* dies with it regardless of exemption. 2. **Foreground service type restrictions (Android 14's biggest change).** Android 14 requires every foreground service to declare a `foregroundServiceType` (camera, microphone, location, mediaPlayback, dataSync, connectedDevice, specialUse, etc.) **and** obtain the matching runtime permission, otherwise `startForeground()` throws. It also banned launching certain FGS types from the background (dataSync, camera, mediaProcessing, phoneCall, etc. must start within a few minutes of a user-triggered event), and added quotas for short-service and dataSync FGS (≈6 hrs/24 hrs). Apps that fail silently or fall back to plain background services get throttled/killed quickly. 3. **Manufacturer "aggressive" memory & battery management (the real culprit on most phones).** MIUI/HyperOS, ColorOS/Realme UI, One UI, OxygenOS/EMUI all run their own task killers that ignore AOSP signals — they kill apps not on their whitelist even when the app is exempted from Doze. OEMs also silently strip `RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED` and alarm wakeups after force-stop. 4. **Exemptions don't stack.** "Unrestricted battery" ≠ exempt from: force-stop, task killers, `KILL_BACKGROUND` from launcher, the 10,000-job / 500-wakeup alarm quotas, or system-initiated LMKD kills. **Workarounds developers actually recommend** - **Prefer push over persistence.** Use FCM high-priority messages to wake the app (whitelisted system path on nearly all OEMs) instead of keeping a resident service (developer.android.com). - **If you must keep alive, use a proper Foreground Service** with a declared `foregroundServiceType` + matching permission, a persistent notification, and on Android 14 the new `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_*` permissions. Use `specialUse` (with justification) or `shortService` for bounded work. - **Chain work with WorkManager / JobScheduler** rather than long-running services — they survive process death and are rescheduled (with constraints: charging, unmetered, etc.). For repeat work, use exact alarms only where justified (`USE_EXACT_ALARM`), otherwise inexact. - **Kill-switch survival:** re-schedule on `BOOT_COMPLETED`, and also on `MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED`. - **Start services from the foreground only** (or within the Android 14 grace window after a user action); starting from a background broadcast will throw `ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException`. - **OEM-specific guidance:** prompt the user to whitelist your app in *each* OEM's task-killer screen (Xiaomi Autostart, Oppo/Realme "Allow background," Samsung "Sleeping apps → Never sleep"), using libraries like **donotkill** or **autostart** helpers to detect the ROM and deep-link to the right settings page. - **Keep the process eligible:** avoid memory-hungry daemons; LMKD kills on memory pressure first — trim caches, use `onTrimMemory` to release resources rather than holding a big footprint. - **Pair FGS with periodic `AlarmManager` re-inflation + WorkManager catch-up** so that if the OEM kills you anyway, work resumes within minutes instead of never. **TL;DR:** Battery-optimization exemption only stops Doze; it doesn't stop LMKD, OEM task killers, or Android 14's FGS type/launch restrictions. The recommended pattern is: FCM/WorkManager as the default, a correctly-typed Foreground Service only for genuinely continuous work, and explicit OEM whitelist prompts as a fallback.

# Complete History of Android Versions (1.0 – 15)

## Overview
Android is an open-source mobile operating system developed by the Open Handset Alliance, led by Google. First released in 2008, Android has grown from a basic smartphone OS into the world's most widely used mobile platform. Below is a complete guide covering every major Android version from 1.0 to 15, including codenames, release years, and major API changes.

---

## Android 1.0 — "Astro" (Astro Boy)
- **Release Year:** 2008 (September)
- **API Level:** 1
- **Key Features:** First commercial release; Home screen with app shortcuts, notifications shade basics, web browser, camera, Gmail integration, Google Maps, YouTube.
- **Major API Changes:** Initial Android SDK; fundamental Activity, Service, Broadcast Receiver, Content Provider framework; basic telephony APIs.
- **Devices:** HTC Dream / T-Mobile G1.

## Android 1.1 — "Bender"
- **Release Year:** 2009 (February)
- **API Level:** 2
- **Key Features:** Minor update; improvements to maps and dialer; long-press behavior on home screen items.
- **Major API Changes:** Small refinements to the initial APIs; no major new subsystems.

## Android 1.5 — "Cupcake"
- **Release Year:** 2009 (April)
- **API Level:** 3
- **Key Features:** On-screen keyboard (replacing physical keyboards), widget support on home screen, video recording (3GP), Bluetooth headset profiles (A2DP), copy-paste in browser.
- **Major API Changes:** Introduction of App Widgets API, Speech-to-text, new `MediaRecorder` capabilities, improved Bluetooth APIs.

## Android 1.6 — "Donut"
- **Release Year:** 2009 (September)
- **API Level:** 4
- **Key Features:** Support for multiple screen resolutions and densities (CDMA phones supported), new Search UI, fast search box, accessibility improvements (TalkBack).
- **Major API Changes:** Support for different screen sizes/densities; improved location APIs; VPN API introduced.

## Android 2.0 / 2.0.1 / 2.1 — "Eclair"
- **Release Year:** 2009 (October – 2010 March)
- **API Level:** 5, 6, 7
- **Key Features:** Redesigned UI, live wallpapers, Microsoft Exchange support, Bluetooth 2.1, turn-by-turn Google Maps navigation, improved camera with flash and digital zoom.
- **Major API Changes:** New contacts API, virtual keyboard refinements, improved camera effects, multi-camera support groundwork.

## Android 2.2 / 2.2.1 — "Froyo" (Frozen Yogurt)
- **Release Year:** 2010 (May)
- **API Level:** 8
- **Key Features:** JIT compiler for major performance boost, Adobe Flash support in browser, portable hotspot (tethering), faster camera, Exchange support improvements.
- **Major API Changes:** Dalvik JIT compiler; new `Cloud-to-device messaging` (precursor to GCM); expanded enterprise device admin APIs.

## Android 2.3 — "Gingerbread"
- **Release Year:** 2010 (December)
- **API Level:** 9, 10 (2.3.3+)
- **Key Features:** Refined UI (dark theme, new color palette), NFC support, improved copy-paste, front-facing camera support, better gaming performance (audio, sensors).
- **Major API Changes:** NFC APIs (`android.nfc`), SIP VoIP APIs, improved Bluetooth and camera APIs, new sensor types, download manager.

## Android 3.0 / 3.1 / 3.2 — "Honeycomb"
- **Release Year:** 2011 (February – July)
- **API Level:** 11, 12, 13
- **Key Features:** Tablet-only release; holographic UI, action bar, Fragments introduced for tablet layouts, system bar with notifications, improved multi-tasking.
- **Major API Changes:** `ActionBar`, Fragments API, new `ActionMode` for contextual actions, USB host/device APIs, Hardware acceleration.

## Android 4.0 — "Ice Cream Sandwich" (ICS)
- **Release Year:** 2011 (October)
- **API Level:** 14, 15 (4.0.3+)
- **Key Features:** Unified phone/tablet UI, Face Unlock, new Roboto typeface, Data Usage settings panel, Chrome-based browser, hardware acceleration default, screenshot support (vol-down + power).
- **Major API Changes:** `Choreographer`, `Transition` framework groundwork, new Bluetooth APIs, improved notifications (inline actions), lock screen widgets groundwork.

## Android 4.1 / 4.2 / 4.3 — "Jelly Bean"
- **Release Year:** 2012 (July – July 2013)
- **API Level:** 16, 17, 18
- **Key Features:** Project Butter (60fps UI), Google Now, expandable notifications, Gesture typing, Miracast support, multiple user profiles (4.2), daydreams/screensaver, quick settings.
- **Major API Changes:** `RenderThread`, lock-screen widgets, daydreams, Text-to-speech improvements, BLE peripheral mode (4.3), `ShortcutManager` groundwork, restricted profile APIs.

## Android 4.4 — "KitKat"
- **Release Year:** 2013 (October)
- **API Level:** 19
- **Key Features:** Immersive mode, translucent system bars, "OK Google" hotword, new status bar icons, Emulator improvements, WebView updates, storage access framework, public Bluetooth PAN.
- **Major API Changes:** Storage Access Framework (`DocumentsProvider`), `Translucent` activities, immersive full-screen, runtime permissions groundwork, `JobScheduler` introduced (API 21 groundwork, but KitKat had precursor job scheduling APIs for print).

## Android 5.0 / 5.1 — "Lollipop"
- **Release Year:** 2014 (November)
- **API Level:** 21, 22
- **Key Features:** Material Design, ART runtime replacing Dalvik, 64-bit support, runtime permissions groundwork (introduced but enforced later), lock screen notifications, Project Volta (battery saver), multiple Bluetooth connections.
- **Major API Changes:** ART replaces Dalvik (AOT compilation), `JobScheduler` API, Material Design components, `Notification` enhancements, TLS by default, 64-bit ABI support.

## Android 6.0 — "Marshmallow"
- **Release Year:** 2015 (October)
- **API Level:** 23
- **Key Features:** Runtime permissions model enforced, Doze mode and App Standby (battery optimization), fingerprint authentication support, Do Not Disturb enhancements, Auto Fill groundwork, USB-C support.
- **Major API Changes:** Runtime permissions (`requestPermissions`), Doze/App Standby APIs, FingerprintManager API, `TextClassifier` groundwork, mobile data nesting support, more granular volume controls.

## Android 7.0 / 7.1 — "Nougat"
- **Release Year:** 2016 (August – October 2016)
- **API Level:** 24, 25
- **Key Features:** Split-screen multi-window, bundled notifications (grouped), Doze on the Go, Data Saver, Vulkan graphics API, seamless system updates (A/B), Daydream VR platform, emoji redesign.
- **Major API Changes:** Multi-window APIs, `NotificationChannel` groundwork (grouped notifications), Doze improvements, `FileProvider`, Vulkan support, JPEG DPI metadata, OpenGL ES 3.2.

## Android 8.0 / 8.1 — "Oreo"
- **Release Year:** 2017 (August – December 2017)
- **API Level:** 26, 27
- **Key Features:** Notification dots, picture-in-picture, adaptive icons, autofill framework, background execution limits, WiFi Aware (Aware), Neural Networks API, Project Treble (modular vendor/system split).
- **Major API Changes:** Background execution limits (implicit broadcast bans, background service restrictions), `NotificationChannel`, `AdaptiveIconDrawable`, `AutofillService`, `Neural Networks API (NNAPI)`, `Vitals` improvements, `WebSocket` improvements.

## Android 9 — "Pie"
- **Release Year:** 2018 (August)
- **API Level:** 28
- **Key Features:** Gesture navigation, Adaptive Battery & Adaptive Brightness (AI/ML), Digital Wellbeing (Dashboard, Wind Down, App Timers), Dashboard, Notch/display cutout support, text selection actions, indoor positioning with Wi-Fi RTT.
- **Major API Changes:** Background activity launch restrictions, `Display cutout` API, Wi-Fi RTT ranging, `Heads-up notification` changes, `Vibration amplitude control`, `Multi-camera` API, DNS-over-TLS, `Java 8 language features` default.

## Android 10 — "Quince Tart" (internally; no public dessert name)
- **Release Year:** 2019 (September)
- **API Level:** 29
- **Key Features:** Dark theme (system-wide), Gesture navigation refinements, Project Mainline (modular updates via Google Play), Privacy controls (scoped storage, location permission granularity: "only while using"), Live Caption, Smart Reply, foldable support, 5G APIs, sharing shortcuts.
- **Major API Changes:** Scoped storage (introduced, enforced in Android 11), runtime permission for background location, `Wi-Fi RTT`, `Neural Networks` improvements, `Platform APIs for foldables` (`Jetpack`/`WindowManager`), sharing shortcuts API, `PermissionController` modularization.

## Android 11 — "Red Velvet Cake" (no public dessert name)
- **Release Year:** 2020 (September)
- **API Level:** 30
- **Key Features:** Chat bubbles, Conversation notifications, One-time permissions, Scoped storage enforcement, Media controls in quick settings, Android Auto wireless, Screen recording built-in, Dark theme scheduling, improved 5G support.
- **Major API Changes:** Background location restricted (must show system dialog), scoped storage enforced, `MediaSession` improvements, `Bluetooth runtime permissions` (nearby devices), `Package visibility` (queries element in manifest), `Safetynet`/API changes, notification policy changes.

## Android 12 — "Snow Cone"
- **Release Year:** 2021 (October)
- **API Level:** 31, 32 (12L for tablets)
- **Key Features:** Material You (dynamic theming with wallpaper-based color palette), redesigned UI, Privacy Dashboard, approximate location permission, clipboard notification, splash screens, improved game performance, scrollable screenshot, AV1 codec support.
- **Major API Changes:** Exact/alarm permissions (`SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM`), Splash screen API, foreground service launch restrictions from background, `MediaButtonReceiver` changes, tighter foreground service types, tighter `PendingIntent` mutability requirements (`FLAG_IMMUTABLE`/`FLAG_MUTABLE` mandatory), Bluetooth runtime permission changes, approximate location only option.

## Android 13 — "Tiramisu"
- **Release Year:** 2022 (August)
- **API Level:** 33
- **Key Features:** Per-app language preferences, Themed app icons (monochrome), Media controls redesign, Notification permission (POST_NOTIFICATIONS runtime permission), QR code scanner built-in, improved Bluetooth LE audio, Photo picker, restrictions on unsafe Bluetooth scanning.
- **Major API Changes:** `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` runtime permission, photo picker (system-provided), per-app language APIs, media keys handled by media session, `Nearby device permission` required for Bluetooth scanning, smarter workspace for large screens (13L/medium).## Android 14 — "Upside Down Cake"
- **Release Year:** 2023 (October)
- **API Level:** 34
- **Key Features:** Partial screen sharing, Health Connect, themed app icons improvements, lock screen customization, predictive back gestures, per-app language improvements, regional preferences (temperature, first day of week), automatic permission management for unused apps.
- **Major API Changes:** Foreground service types **required** (`foregroundServiceType` must be declared and permission-matched), background FGS launch restrictions (dataSync, camera, etc.), runtime-permission requirements for FGS types, 64-bit-only requirement for new apps (Play Store), openJDK 17 language features, restricted implicit intents, non-SDK interface tightening, `Secure background activity launches`.

## Android 15 — "Vanilla Ice Cream"
- **Release Year:** 2024 (October, stable release)
- **API Level:** 35
- **Key Features:** Large-screen/foldable optimizations, partial screen-sharing improvements, satellite support (messaging), Health Connect improvements, privacy changes (restricting access to some system properties), app archiving, edge-to-edge enforced by default, improved thermal API, PDF UI improvements.
-**Major API Changes:** Edge-to-edge enforced by default (targetSdk 35), `Bluetooth Quality`/`LE Audio` improvements, restricted Sensitive system properties, `Media` API improvements, refined foreground-service time limits, partial screen sharing media projection changes, `JobScheduler`/`WorkManager` refinements, notification cooldown (reduces notification sounds), private space.
